facts.fact: The World Bank's status report says the Rokhas digital platform for issuing building permits and commercial licences is operational and publicly accessible in all participating municipalities (100 per cent against a target of 50), on the latest information from the Interior Ministry's DGCT; it names the platform, not the municipalities' connection.

The World Bank's status report says Rokhas has been deployed in over 91 participating municipalities covering 16.9 million people, as verified by the independent verification agent since about 2022; elsewhere it counts 117 participating municipalities, and it gives no national total of municipalities.

The World Bank's status report says the integrated revenue management system (GIR-CT) is implemented in 70 per cent of participating municipalities as verified by the independent verification agent, and that DGCT confirmed at the mid-term review that it operates in all of them.

The World Bank's status report says the back-office system for the civil registry is operational in 59 of 97 participating municipalities (61 per cent), as verified by the Interior Ministry's inspectorate IGAT.

The World Bank's status report counts 59 of 97 participating municipalities with the civil registry back-office system operational, as verified by IGAT; the denominator is the programme's participating municipalities, not the country's.

The World Bank's status report gives the Interior Ministry's directorate for local governments (DGCL/DGCT) as responsible for the programme under which the digital platforms GIR-CT, Rokhas, civil registry and Chikaya were rolled out to participating municipalities, and as the source confirming they operate.
facts.system: Municipal Performance Program digital platforms (GIR-CT, Rokhas, civil registry, Chikaya)

facts.fact: The World Bank's status report says the Municipal Performance Program, whose third sub-programme rolled out the digital platforms, is financed by an IBRD loan of which EUR 192 million (71 per cent) has been disbursed, with AFD co-financing, and closes on 31 December 2026; it states no domestic budget line for the platforms.

The facts rest on the typology's rule that working in a shared system held elsewhere is evidence of a connection: the report states platforms operational in municipalities and never states an office connection, its type or who pays for it.
